Funny thing about “broken Obamacare” claims…

Premiums did rise under the ACA but so did coverage, protections for pre-existing conditions, and insurer profits. That’s why Congress spent years backfilling costs with subsidies instead of fixing the underlying pricing structure.

Expanding options can help at the margins. But short term plans, association plans, and choice language don’t change hospital consolidation, drug pricing power, or the fact that Congress delayed structural reform while costs climbed.

If this bill truly lowers premiums, Americans should be able to see where, how much, and for whom not just slogans after a late night vote.

Healthcare didn’t break overnight, and it won’t be fixed by jogging videos.

Results will tell the story.
